deviations.description: 1.6.1 forest on the standardized latent against the v2 forest on the raw latent
deviations.explanation: 1.6.1 standardizes the latent before the forest, v2 does not. Splits are invariant to the monotone rescaling; only rounding of the split thresholds can change a prediction.
deviations.name: forest/scaled_predictions

findings: 1.6.1 `RandomForest` passes no `random_state`, so every 1.6.1 forest is unseeded and not reproducible. v2 `RandomForestPredictor` defaults to `random_state=42` (as the plan asks), which also changes `singleDrugRandomForest` and `MultiViewRandomForest`. Parity is shown by seeding the 1.6.1 global state with `np.random.seed(42)` before the fit, which equals `RandomState(42)`.

Parity holds with `n_jobs=1`. The preset keeps `n_jobs=-1` (as 1.6.1); with several workers the predictions differ by one ulp from the sequential run, because the per-tree predictions are summed in a different order.

1.6.1 `SklearnModel.train` standardizes the encoder latent (`scale_gene_expression`, fitted on the unique training samples) before the forest; v2 passes the raw latent. A tree split is invariant to a monotone per-feature rescaling, so only floating-point rounding of the thresholds can differ (deviation step `forest/scaled`).

1.6.1 applies `log2(clip(x, 0) + 1)` to the TPM datasets by *name* (CCLE, CTRPv1, CTRPv2) and nothing else; v2 decides from the `expression_unit` of the view (`linear` -> log2), so a log-scale dataset is never transformed twice. Unlike DIPK there is no per-sample z-score in either version. Not exercised here: the case feeds the already log-scale matrices.
v2 holds features as float32 end to end; the case uses float32-representable inputs so both sides see the same numbers.

The v2 encoder cache key is a superset of the 1.6.1 one (config, input width, sorted train and validation sample ids, gene-order hash) and adds a sha256 of the train and validation matrices, so an edited expression matrix under unchanged ids cannot hit a stale encoder. The env var is still `DREVAL_AE_CACHE`. Cache IO is not part of this case.
The v2 MolGNet featurizer pools per drug instead of through a stacked node array, so drugs with equal atom counts cannot collapse the node matrices to a 3-D array.
